segments.t: In the dining room of Arcobaleno, the guest introduces himself to Viktor and reveals that he knows all about Viktor's drunken crash into Claude Monet's owner. Listen to the Russian scene first.
Чего надо, любезный?
Представиться, познакомиться.
Знаете, между нами, я вами восхищаюсь.
Я серьёзно.
Сесть в машину и проехаться по хозяину ресторана.
Подожди, я здесь уже.
Да здесь я, здесь, дорогая.
Сейчас буду, не волнуйся.
Вы хоть хозяина Аркабалено не задавите, а?
А то ведь уволят. И Елена Павловна не поможет.
Слышь ты! Хотя ты прав, не поможет.
Прямо расцеловал бы тебя, да боюсь замараться.
Let's break this conversation down line by line.
Чего надо, любезный?
'What do you want, my good man?' In spoken Russian, the words stay in their normal statement order and Chef Barinov's rising voice at the end turns the line into a question.
Представиться, познакомиться.
'To introduce myself and get acquainted.' Here German anchors the thought on 'to introduce oneself' and finishes on 'to get acquainted, to meet', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Знаете, между нами, я вами восхищаюсь.
'You know, between us, I admire you.' In everyday Russian, 'know' flows straight into 'to admire, be delighted with' without extra linking words.
Я серьёзно.
'I am completely serious.' German uses the first-person pronoun in the case required by the Russian verb or preposition.
Сесть в машину и проехаться по хозяину ресторана.
'To get in a car and run over the owner of the restaurant.' Notice how Russian puts 'to sit down' and 'restaurant' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Подожди, я здесь уже.
'Wait, I am already here.' Here Max anchors the thought on 'wait' and finishes on 'already', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Да здесь я, здесь, дорогая.
'Yes, I am here, right here, darling.' Spoken Russian keeps this brief and expressive, built right around 'dear' without extra helper words.
Сейчас буду, не волнуйся.
'I will be right there, don't worry.' German pairs 'right now' with 'worry' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Вы хоть хозяина Аркабалено не задавите, а?

'At least don't run over the owner of Arcobaleno, huh?' Putting the short word for 'not' right in front of the action word is all Russian needs to make a sentence negative, with no extra helper words like 'do' or 'did'.
А то ведь уволят. И Елена Павловна не поможет.
'Otherwise they will fire you. And Elena Pavlovna won't be able to help.' Here German anchors the thought on 'will fire' and finishes on 'will help', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Слышь ты! Хотя ты прав, не поможет.
'Listen here! Though you are right, she won't help.' In everyday Russian, 'listen' flows straight into 'will help' without extra linking words.
Прямо расцеловал бы тебя, да боюсь замараться.

'I would kiss you right now, for giving me that idea, if I weren't afraid of getting dirty.' Chef Barinov pairs 'right, straight' with 'to getting' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'. Now listen to the full Russian exchange again with everything in place.

Now you have heard Viktor's first encounter with German Mikhailovich in the dining room of Arcobaleno. Pay attention to the ironic politeness in their exchange. Until next time!
